body:
Adds tests inside the browser app that prove the document-config hand-off: they fail when the config every browser document loads with is replaced by a default, or when its network provider or its navigation provider is dropped.
The same tests read, through that config's own navigation provider, that a remote page's navigation to a file: URL loads nothing while a file: page's navigation does.
These kill the three mutation survivors the Epoch 4 code audit measured in that function; a cargo-mutants run on the document loader re-measures the kill once the host is free.
It also writes a justification beside two bare expect_used allows in the browser app, the favicon test module's and the tab web view's. It changes no browser behaviour.

body_fields.what: the browser's document loader, which builds the document config (network provider, navigation provider holding the page URL) every browser document loads with — edits: tests of make_doc_config
the browser's favicon loading and its test module — edits: the test module's expect_used allow, given a written reason
the browser tab and its web view component — edits: the TabWebView expect_used allow, given a written reason

body: The document config the browser builds for each document: tests must show it is the built config and not a default, and that it carries both its network provider and its navigation provider.

The navigation provider's document URL is the page URL the file: navigation gate reads. The tests must show, through the config's own provider, that a remote page loads no file: URL and a file: page does.

Restructure invariant: no browser behaviour changes. The hand-off and the file: navigation gate stay as the remote-pages-local-files chunk built them. The chunk adds only tests and justification text, and the browser's existing tests keep holding them.

The config builder reads a shell provider from the Dioxus context, so its tests run inside a Dioxus runtime (a virtual DOM) that provides that context, the same way the browser's history tests run navigation.
Every clippy expect_used allow in the browser app carries a written justification, as a comment beside it or as the allow's reason. The favicon test module's exception then lapses.
The new tests run in the workspace test leg and are CI-gated. The mutation tier is a dev-host run and not a CI leg.
Scope bound: the browser app only. No engine crate, driver, carrier, verb, field, log site or span changes.
Accessibility tree construction, role mapping, accessible names and ARIA state or property reads: the chunk builds and reads no accessibility tree.
Keyboard navigation, focus, activation, and select, range or grid key contracts: the chunk adds no input handling.
Contrast, visual lint findings, select list colours, scrollbar and stand visual rules: the chunk paints nothing and measures no colour.
Snapshot, snapshot text and diff, actions answer, driver refusals, screenshots, MCP results and UI graph rows: the chunk touches no driver or agent reader.
Stand expectation tables, stand tab order, stand contrast assertions and the stand's three-round checks: the chunk touches no stand app.
Platform adapter, AccessKit adapter wiring, accessibility feature defaults and Dioxus accessibility feature selection: the chunk changes no feature or adapter.
Cognitive accessibility rules (invalid state beyond colour or class): the chunk renders no form state.

**2026-11-14-remote-pages-local-files** (Conventions, amd-4nm4q3gr) — `~ decision/justified-expect-unwrap` except narrowed from "the browser app's test module" to "the browser app's favicon test module", because history.rs's new test module stood beside a justification. This chunk writes the favicon test module's justification (favicon.rs:76) and tab.rs:178's, so the except names no exception any more and the wrap's reconcile drops it. tab.rs's TabWebView allow was never named in the except, so the row was already silently contradicted (the cry-775jieku CARRY).

**2026-11-14-remote-pages-local-files** (Standard Contracts, amd-jdzhcam4) — `~ decision/file-url-load-rule`: in the browser app, a navigation that a non-`file:` page starts to a `file:` URL is not a top-level load and is dropped silently. The navigation provider drops it and loads and logs nothing. This chunk's tests prove exactly that gate through `make_doc_config`'s navigation provider: a remote page's `file:` navigation loads nothing and a `file:` page's does. The rule must stay as built (Boundaries: no behaviour change).

**2026-11-14-remote-pages-local-files** (Established Decisions, amd-wa4jxqrv) — `~ decision/sub-resource-requests-carry-initiator`: a request with no initiator is now "the user's own load, or a navigation its page may start", no longer any navigation. This is the companion of the gate that `BrowserNavProvider::for_document(history, base_url)` feeds through its `document_url`. The new tests rest on this split between user loads and page-started navigations.

**2026-11-13-local-files-for-local-documents** (Established Decisions, amd-tbrxc4nl) — `~ decision/url-scheme-routing`: `file:` is read from disk only for a top-level load or a `file:` loading document and is otherwise refused before any disk read. `~ decision/file-script-load-refused` and `+ decision/sub-resource-requests-carry-initiator` were also added. This is the engine half of the gate whose browser-side hand-off this chunk proves. The net_provider in `make_doc_config` is the path these refusals ride on.

**2026-11-13-local-files-for-local-documents** (Standard Contracts, amd-y3dq25xu) — `~ decision/file-url-load-rule` widened from script loads to every engine request. blitz-net refuses with FileForbidden before reading the disk, and top-level loads are exempt. It also added `contract/blitz-traits-net/request-initiator` and `contract/stylesheet-handler/document-url`. This is the row history this chunk's tests must read consistently: a remote page's navigation loads nothing.

**2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** (`document_may_load`, amd-xyrrgurw) — registered the public `document_may_load(document_url, url)`, re-exported from blitz-vibey-script's crate root, and `FetchError::Forbidden`, and recorded the change as a narrowing, not a widening. These are the origin of `contract/blitz-vibey-script-api/document-may-load`, `contract/script/document-may-load` and `contract/script-fetcher/errors`. `history.rs` `navigate_to` asks this same predicate, and the chunk's tests read its answer through the config's navigation provider.

**2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** (`TMPDIR` test-only site, amd-6yml6hnj) — registered blitz-vibey-script's `temp_dir_with_files`, which writes `file:` fixtures under the system temp dir (`$TMPDIR/…`, test code only). Its tests are `remote_document_cannot_load_file_urls` and `file_document_can_load_sibling_file_urls`. This is the precedent for remote-versus-`file:` pair tests. If the new browser tests touch the disk, they need the same test-only registration; a URL-only test needs none.

**2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** (browser tab lenses, amd-hfn4sexj; tab.rs citations, amd-764rqx7s) — added the browser-app decision block (`tab_lens_survives_webview_props_replacement`, upstream's, upstream-only app) and stretched the `tab.rs` chrome-write citation to `:126-154`. This history touches `apps/browser/src/tab.rs`, where this chunk writes the TabWebView allow's justification (`:178`). The edit is comment-only, but any line shift moves those citations.

**2026-10-24-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship** (`Parallel` style traversals, amd-ifh4aulq) — records that the browser's document loader and toolbar build their documents with `style_threading: Parallel`, serialised process-wide by `PARALLEL_TRAVERSAL_LOCK`, so two documents no longer panic. `make_doc_config` in `document_loader.rs` is that builder. A test that builds a config or document in process should know `Parallel` is the browser's setting and that the lock is process-wide state.

**2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship** (default sheet from the config, amd-w3z3f3db) — `DocumentConfig`'s hand-written `Default` now carries the one default user-agent sheet (`ua_stylesheets: Vec<UserAgentStylesheet>`), and a config that sets the field is used as given. This is the shape behind `contract/document-core/documentconfig` and `decision/document-config`. The chunk's first mutation survivor is "the config replaced by a default", so its test must tell `make_doc_config`'s result from `DocumentConfig::default()`. A Default with no providers has `net_provider`/`navigation_provider` at their no-op `Dummy*` defaults (`decision/embedder-services-default-noop`).

**2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock** (Document core, amd-3rlakvkd) — `DocumentConfig` gained `clock: Option<Arc<dyn Clock>>`, `None` in `Default`. This was the last change to the field list that `contract/document-core/documentconfig` states (viewport, providers, sheets, fonts, media, threading, incremental, abort, depth, clock). A test comparing the browser's config against a default should read the provider fields it means to pin, not compare the whole struct.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (`NetHandler::error`, amd-4suux6zc) — a trait default method that does nothing hid a fix behind a wrapper (`CountedHandler`). The recorded trap: a do-nothing default compiles silently, so the implementers of an extended trait must be swept. This is the same hazard this chunk's survivors show: deleting `net_provider` or `navigation_provider` from `make_doc_config` falls back to the no-op provider defaults (`decision/injected-embedder-services`, `contract/provider-traits/shellprovider`, `contract/net-provider/is-noop`) and stays green unless a test reads the injected provider.

**2026-10-16-fast-failing-mutants** (mutation tier host instruments, amd-5hxke3kf) — set up the source of `decision/mutation-tier-host-only` and `decision/nextest-mutants-profile`: cargo-mutants with `--test-tool nextest` under the `mutants` profile of `.config/nextest.toml`, run on the dev host only and never in CI, with each unit's mutant test command read green on the unmutated tree first. The survivors' kill on `document_loader.rs` is read by such a host run once the host is free; it is no CI leg.

**2026-11-15-upstream-sync-errors-and-explanation** (Stack and Technologies, amd-fijsdyn4) — `+ decision/mutation-tier-excludes-demo-shells`: the founder ruled two test-less demo units out of the mutation tier, and the code audit reads its extra exclusions only from an architecture decision row. The browser app is not excluded: its score of 50.0 and its three survivors stand in scope, which this chunk kills.

**2026-10-05-fork-ci-reached** (fork CI through one leg script, amd-gh222uio) — the origin of `decision/one-ci-leg-runner`, `contract/ci-leg-legs/test`, `contract/ci-leg-script/exit-status` and `decision/linux-tested-by-fast-leg`. Every linux job runs `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh {leg}`, whose `test` leg runs the workspace tests, and the matrix tests only windows and macos. The browser app's new tests are CI-gated through the workspace `test` leg, the `[inferred]` boundary P3 closes.

**2026-11-12T03-36-23-rows** (the masters as rows, amd-yhg3j6hb) — the master's text became the rows this chunk is bound by, each verified against the code. That conversion created the duplicate pairs among the picked rows (`decision/justified-expect-unwrap` / `decision/unwrap-expect-justified`; `decision/clippy-allow-scoping` / `decision/local-lint-allows`; `decision/net-feature-noop-on-wasm` / `decision/net-noop-on-wasm`). When the wrap drops the favicon exception, it must reconcile every twin that states the expect/unwrap rule.

body: The DocumentConfig hand-off: the document configuration struct a browser document is built from must carry the embedder's net provider and the navigation provider the browser builds for that document; the new tests must fail when the config is a default, when the net provider is dropped and when the navigation provider is dropped.

The navigation provider's document URL is the page URL the file: navigation gate reads: file URLs load only for file documents, so a remote page's navigation to a file: URL loads nothing while a file: page's navigation to one does; the tests read this through the config's own navigation provider, via the document_may_load answer the gate uses.

Embedder services are injected with no-op defaults: a default DocumentConfig carries the no-op net provider and the default navigation provider, so a test tells the browser's config from a default by what its providers report (the net provider's is_noop, the navigation provider's document URL).

The config builder consumes the ShellProvider from the Dioxus root contexts, so a test of it runs inside a Dioxus runtime that provides a ShellProvider context, as the browser's history tests run navigation inside a VirtualDom; the harness shape is closed in P3.

expect and unwrap need a justification: every clippy expect_used allow in the browser app carries a written reason beside it, a comment line or the allow's reason field, and the new tests' own expect or unwrap calls carry one too; the rule's exception naming the favicon test module then names nothing and is dropped at the wrap's reconcile.

Clippy allows are kept local and lints allowed locally: the justifications stand on the existing scoped allows, the favicon test module's and TabWebView's, and no allow is widened to a crate or file level.

The mutation tier is host-run, no CI leg: the kill of the three survivors (the config replaced by a default, the net provider deleted, the navigation provider deleted) is read by a cargo-mutants run on the document loader under the nextest mutants profile, once the host is free; the browser app's mutation score is re-measured by it.
The new browser tests run in the workspace test leg of the CI leg runner and are CI-gated there; P3 closes it against the leg script and the workspace members.

The chunk adds tests and justification text only, in the browser app alone: no new public item, carrier, verb, field, log site or span, and the shell and navigation providers keep their present shape.

body_fields.convention: each new test carries a descriptive name saying the behaviour it proves
each new unit test sits in the test module at the end of the source file it tests, placed as the unit-test placement rule says
each new test asserts its fixture's precondition first, before the behaviour it proves
each new test module and test passes the formatting and clippy gate and the rustdoc warnings gate, and carries the module docs a new module owes

**2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship** — §Surface: desktop-native → Tokens: the user-agent-sheet line changed from `DioxusDocument::new`'s own `DEFAULT_CSS` call to "every document gets it once, through `DocumentConfig::default()` (`UserAgentStylesheet::default_sheet()`)", after upstream #1189 removed the call; the founder confirmed it on 2026-10-13. This is where the picked row `decision/default-ua-sheet-via-default-config` comes from. `make_doc_config` builds the browser's `DocumentConfig`, so the chunk's tests that fail "when the config is replaced by a default" must not cut the sheet off. The browser config has to keep taking the sheet through the default (for example `..Default::default()`). Pinned by `default_config_uses_the_default_sheet`.

**2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** (citations follow the script runtime's split and the taken commits' line moves) — moved the line range of the `apps/browser/src/tab.rs` citation for the 16x16 favicon after upstream added lines to `tab.rs`. **2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — §Surface: desktop-native, Platform-Specific Notes: code the vdom runs during a render on every Dioxus document can call `MountedData` with no `RefCell already borrowed` panic. The render is buffered and then replayed under one borrow, so a call made during a render acts on the document as the previous render left it. The chunk's `make_doc_config` test has to run inside a Dioxus runtime (a `VirtualDom` that provides a `ShellProvider` context). This note sets the borrow and render-timing limits such a harness inherits; the test must not depend on reading a document mid-render.

body: The document config hand-off: every browser document loads with a config that carries a network provider and a navigation provider built for that document from its history and page URL. New tests prove that neither provider can be dropped and that the config cannot be swapped for the default config.

The file: navigation gate, re-asserted and not changed: through the config's navigation provider, a remote page's navigation to a file: URL loads nothing, and a file: page's navigation to a file: URL loads.
The page URL a document's navigation provider reports is the value the navigation gate reads to decide whether a document may load. The tests read it as the gate reads it.

Indirect, through the shell provider: building the document config reads the shell provider from the Dioxus context, so a test of it runs inside a Dioxus runtime (a virtual DOM) that provides a shell provider. P3 settles the harness shape.

The browser tab's web view component: its expect_used allow gets a written reason. The tab's other allows, and the history's, already stand beside a comment and stay as they are.

**2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** — (the `file:` refusal in the script error surface; the take read at `ebacd68bd` silent) This entry is the origin of the no-file-loads row: `document_may_load` refuses a file: load from a non-file: document with no log site of its own. It also set the precedent that the file:-refusal tests `remote_document_cannot_load_file_urls` and `file_document_can_load_sibling_file_urls` were recorded as an observed-absent row (no print or log site), their one census hit being a test-only `TMPDIR` read through `std::env::temp_dir()`. The row binds the browser app's new tests: no subscriber, no env read, no print, readings into assertions only. The network provider the test hands in or reads is a hand-written stand-in that keeps its loads counted, and the test reaches no network: the remote page URL is a value stated in code, no request leaves the host.
Test data stated in code: page URLs and file: URLs the tests use are literals in the test, nothing seeded on disk beyond what the test itself states.
The new tests sit in an inline test module in their source file and run on Rust's built-in test harness, so they run in the workspace test leg and are CI-gated.

Justified expect/unwrap: every expect_used allow in the browser app stands beside a written justification (a comment line or the allow's reason); the favicon test module's and the tab webview's allows gain theirs, so the rule's except over the favicon test module then names no exception. Any expect the new tests use falls under an allow that carries its reason.
The new test code passes the workspace clippy leg, the expect_used lint included, with no new bare allow.

No behaviour change, the invariant: the hand-off (the document config with its network and navigation providers) and the file: navigation gate stand as the remote-pages-local-files chunk built them; its existing gate tests still hold them, and the justification edits change no code path.

The new tests document the survivors they kill: each names or states the mutation it guards against (config defaulted, network provider dropped, navigation provider dropped), as a regression test documents its bug.
No sleep or wall-clock read in the new tests: any wait on the virtual DOM is driven, never timed.
A failing assertion in the new tests prints no argument value beyond fixed text: no page URL or path echoed beyond what the test itself states.

The cold-agent pipe and agent-run — their verbs, events, exit codes, verdict and state: the chunk adds no harness run and no agent check.
The engine harness's lint defects, text contrast, screenshot and pixel tests, layout modes and paint expectations: no engine crate, no rendering change.
The seven_guis headless stand — its boot, timer, load page and stand-repeat rounds: the chunk adds no stand check.
Recorded checks, check replay and handler coverage: the chunk records and replays no check.

The CI helper scripts' own contracts — the apt-install script's exit codes, the coverage floor script's exit codes, CI artifacts and log names, CI action pinning, secrets and permissions: the chunk adds no CI job or script.
